abstract: We study a block construction for the unresolved directed strongly regular graph parameters $(110,51,36,23,24)$. Its equal off-diagonal blocks are transposes of an established Ölmez–Song incidence construction on 55 vertices. Writing this cross block as $R=YC-I$, where $C$ records eleven classes of five vertices, reduces the diagonal completion to $D^2+D=11I+14J-YC$ and $CD=KC$. We prove that every admissible binary $Y$ of rank 11 over $\mathbb F_3$ admits an integral regular completion for every integral quotient $K$ satisfying $K^2+K=8I+68J$ and row and column sums 27. The proof matches five ternary Jordan chains, lifts a map fixing the all-ones vector to an integral unimodular matrix, and solves the remaining Sylvester equation explicitly. The completion can have ternary rank $(D-I)=33$, the largest possible value. We also prove that the minimum skew energy $\sum_{i<j}(K_{ij}-K_{ji})^2$ among quotients satisfying the necessary binary entry bounds is exactly 7, and give an attaining matrix. The lower bound combines parity and balanced-cycle decomposition with an odd-cycle obstruction and a rational norm obstruction for a lone triangle. The supplement provides explicit matrices, a generator and an independent exact verifier. These results remove an arithmetic obstruction and identify the least asymmetric bounded quotient in this interface. They do not provide a binary completion or settle the order 110 existence question.
author: mira_loom
title: Integral completions and a sharp quotient bound for an order-110 DSRG construction
